title: Thermally drawn multimaterial fibers as one-dimensional memory substrates
idea: TRIZ #17 Another dimension: replace the 2D wafer with a 1D substrate. A macroscopic preform of chalcogenide-glass semiconductor, polymer dielectric and metal electrodes is thermally drawn into kilometres of fiber whose cross-section is one memory column (bitline, storage electrodes, access channel); fibers are then woven or laminated with orthogonal wordline fibers into 3D blocks.
why: Capital intensity (Fact 4): draw towers make kilometres per hour with no lithography, and wide-gap chalcogenides give low leakage (Fact 3); density and speed are highly speculative.
note: Litho-free km-scale drawn fiber columns woven into 3D blocks; doubt: fiber feature sizes and chalcogenide speed far from DRAM density.

title: Self-assembled diode dots: block copolymers replace EUV for every cell
idea: Inverts 'lithography must define each access device': coat a PS-b-PDMS block copolymer guided by coarse 193 nm trenches into 10 nm-pitch dot arrays, then convert each dot by sequential infiltration synthesis into a vertical oxide Schottky diode atop a MIM nanocapacitor, mapping out defective dots at test.
why: Zero EUV layers (fact 4) and ~1 mask per tier at 10 nm pitch; with 8 tiers, ~100x lower cost per GB; trade-off is diode leakage forcing ms refresh and DSA defect remapping.
note: EUV-free 10 nm-pitch stacked tiers; doubts: DSA defectivity, SIS diode rectification, diode-access leakage.

title: Ephemeral RAM: leaky poly-Si cells for data that dies young
idea: IFR: the data dies before the bit does. Define an ephemeral memory class with 0.5-2 ms retention made of cheap, leaky poly-Si 2T0C gain cells stacked in NAND-style tiers, and have the accelerator runtime map only activations, gradients and KV blocks with measured lifetimes under a millisecond onto it, so refresh is never issued.
why: Constraint: accepting poor leakage buys NAND-like stacking cost, >10x density at about the same wafer cost, with zero refresh for the large short-lived share of accelerator traffic.
note: Accept ms retention to get cheap stacked poly-Si gain cells for short-lived AI data; doubt: 2T0C NAND-like stacking density claim.

title: Millefiori glass-cane draw sliced into litho-free vertical access arrays
idea: Assemble a cm-scale preform holding ~10^4 coaxial access-transistor cross-sections (chalcogenide-glass semiconductor core, glass gate dielectric, low-melting metal gate). Thermally draw it 10^4x as Venetian millefiori cane or optical fiber is drawn, then slice 100 nm discs: each slice is a ready-made array of vertical gate-all-around access switches.
why: Capital intensity and fact 4: removes the EUV patterning of the access layer altogether. A wide-gap glassy channel gives low off-current, and one draw tower replaces scanners for this layer.
note: Multimaterial fiber draw (Fink lab) sliced into GAA access arrays; doubts: 10 nm uniformity, chalcogenide channel quality, contacting slices.

title: Accordion-folded single membrane becomes 26 tiers of crystalline cells
idea: Process one planar single-crystal membrane (SOI device layer) with lateral access transistors in a strip pattern, release it, then fold it accordion-style like a road map using prestressed hinge lines. N folds yield N tiers that all came from one high-quality planar process.
why: Fact 2: gives 3D DRAM single-crystal lateral transistors for every tier while using only planar processing once. Folding replaces 26x deposition/etch loops.
note: Folding gives tiers but no dense inter-tier contacts or nm alignment; micron tier pitch caps density.

title: Thousand-times-leakier cells tamed by a refresh engine per tile
idea: Inverts 'access transistors must leak <=13 fA': use the cheapest stackable access devices (unannealed sputtered poly-Si or oxide TFTs leaking ~10 pA) so retention is only ~10-100 us, and put a micro-sense-amp under each 4k-cell tile (CMOS-under-array) that refreshes its own tile continuously without touching global bitlines.
why: Trades refresh energy (~3-5x today) for ~100x lower cost per GB from low-temperature, 2-mask tiers with no deep capacitor; refresh traffic never leaves the tile, so bandwidth is unaffected.
note: Cheap stacked TFT tiers; doubt: 1000x refresh rate makes standby energy dominant.

title: Float-glass style liquid-gallium printing of atomically thin Ga2O3 channels
idea: As float glass forms on molten tin, kiss the wafer against a liquid Ga/In alloy. Its self-limiting 1.5-3 nm oxide skin transfers at room temperature as a crystalline wide-gap 2D channel for BEOL access transistors.
why: Eg ~4.8 eV in an atomically thin channel could push off-current below 1e-21 A per cell (beyond IGZO). It is BEOL-stackable for 3D with no epitaxy tool, aiming for >100x less refresh.
note: Room-temperature transfer of Ga2O3 skin from liquid metal as BEOL channel; wafer-scale uniformity and contacts are open.

title: Four-pocket mirror-bit storage on both faces of channel sheets
idea: IFR: one gate crossing holds four bits. Each wordline crossing of a thin vertical oxide-semiconductor sheet stores charge in four spatially separate nitride-nanodot pockets (source-side and drain-side on front and back faces, with independent front and back gates), read by swapping source/drain direction as in mirror-bit NROM.
why: Constraint: 4 bits per crossing x 8 cheap tiers is ~20x bits per footprint versus 6F^2, leaving margin for ≥10x per dollar after process overhead.
note: NROM-style charge trapping has ~1e5 endurance and slow program; fails DRAM-class endurance even if density gain holds.

title: Series-gated shared read channel: NAND-string gain cells
idea: IFR: many bits, one read transistor. Make 8-16 storage nodes the consecutive gate segments of a single vertical read channel; to read node k, plate lines capacitively boost every other node above threshold so the string current reports only node k's charge, while tiny vertical oxide write devices fill each node.
why: Constraint: per-bit read transistors and contacts disappear and 16 bits share one hole footprint, ~10x density at 3D NAND-like cost; non-destructive read also removes fact 8's restore writeback.
note: Sixteen storage gates on one read channel remove per-bit read FETs; per-node write devices and 3D wiring are unsolved.

title: Eliminate the incumbents' data monopoly: open 1-um access-device PDK across universities
idea: Publish an open process kit for 100 mm wafer access devices (Si, SiC, Ga2O3 variants) runnable in ten U.S. university nanofabs, each running monthly shuttles with standardized retention-tail test structures; pooled data on millions of cells reveal which elimination (junction, oxide, body) shrinks the tail.
why: Breaks the barrier that only three firms see leakage-tail statistics at scale; accelerates U.S. access-device innovation for ~$10M/yr instead of a $15B fab.

title: Light-pumped self-restoring cell: photodiode gated by its own charge
idea: Box: cap x Si access nMOS x SA x backside-illuminated die under a uniform LED/laser sheet x thinned Si x BSI image-sensor process. Each cell adds a photodiode in series with a tiny transistor gated by the storage node, so a global light flash tops up only nodes that are already high, refreshing the whole array in parallel without any row activation.
why: Refresh energy/bandwidth (fact 3) moves from ~46 fJ/bit bitline CV2 to a few fJ/bit of photons with zero activations, also removing refresh-driven hammer (fact 9). Stray photocurrent into 0-nodes is the risk.
note: Light-driven, self-gated top-up refreshes the whole array with zero activations; doubts: photodiode area per cell, stray photocurrent into 0-nodes.

title: Threshold-switch crossbar capacitors: 64 decks, refreshed constantly
idea: Inverts 'an access device must hold the bit for 64 ms': put a chalcogenide ovonic threshold switch in series with a tiny MIM capacitor at every crossbar node, stack 64 self-aligned decks with two KrF masks each, accept us-to-ms retention set by OTS leakage, and refresh whole decks in parallel from base CMOS.
why: 4F2 per deck with no transistor or EUV, ~100x cheaper per GB; trade-off is refresh power (~20-40% of total), half-select disturb and OTS drift.
note: us retention means ~1000x refresh rate; refresh power likely dominates, not 20-40%.
